- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for spikes.
- After a strong upward spike in history, model often overshoots downward; apply a downward bias of 1–3% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model tends to overestimate; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- If sentiment turns bearish mid-period (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 2–3 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- When sentiment is uniformly negative (e.g., 18/18 = 0.00), model often underestimates true drop; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to avoid under-shock.
